editorial:
Imagine walking into a hotel that looks normal on the outside, but inside it is a giant trap filled with hidden rooms and gas pipes meant to kill you. H. Holmes built in Chicago during the 1893 World's Fair. You get to dive deep into the life of a man who was basically a professional liar and a monster. The movie feels like a dark history lesson that keeps you on edge because it shows how easy it was for him to trick people into trusting him. It sets a creepy mood from the start and makes you wonder how someone could be so cruel.

What really works here is how the film connects the dots between Holmes and other famous killers. The pacing is steady, though some parts feel a bit slow since it relies on old photos and interviews. If you love true crime, you will find the details about the murder castle fascinating. It is a great pick for anyone who likes a good scare based on real life.
endingExplained: The film wraps up by showing how Holmes finally got caught after his scams fell apart. It explains his trial and the eventual execution that ended his reign of terror. The big twist is the theory that Holmes might have actually been Jack the Ripper, traveling to London to kill. It leaves you thinking about whether he was the most dangerous man of his time or just a very lucky killer who finally ran out of time.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves real life horror stories and true crime documentaries.
